doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Phone calls, then getting the Regis Philbin show gig after Steve Allen
summary: Gibbs, a friend of Steve Allen, was hired as musical director for Regis Philbin's show on a 26-week contract.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Edit You ever get these crank phone calls saying —
They are my biggest fans. I get calls all the time, I mean I can’t sign autographs.
Right. So you had mentioned that you rarely had to seek out new things to do, that the phone would ring, like that, except it would be someone with an offer to do something.

And I admire that and so I wanted to talk about your TV band days. I’m imagining that that was a pressure situation. Like, okay Terry, tomorrow we’ve got this certain guest and they want this theme, and have it ready. Is that correct?

Well I’ll tell you how it all started. I used to be — Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine, you know. And when he got his TV show he got me as a guest all the time, I was a guest a lot. And we were doing the show in California and I did his show with them and one of the producers, he loved me. He loved my dumb sense of humor, because I’m not a comedian but I’ve got the wit sort of like Steve’s. Steve loved me because, for example, if he did a comedy bit with Jonathan Winters and he wanted to use the band, about four or five of the guys had to get a line or two, he’d give everybody a script with a line. He wouldn’t give me a script. He would tell me to improvise — and let me ad lib my line. Because he loved my sense of humor. So anyhow, I was back in New York City, Gerry, my son Gerry was just born. And I get a call, I was living in New York, from California from the producer saying that Steve Allen just had a fight with Westinghouse and quit and they’re bringing this young kid in called Regis Philbin who was completely unknown. In fact the first review we ever got said, “What’s a Regis Philbin?” Nobody said — because the name was so odd, Regis Philbin. So he said, “I’d like you to come in and see what kind of rapport — and I’d like you to be musical director.” I was never a music director, but when I did TV shows I always saw what the producer did. I was interested in how it worked, how they put things out. Would he give Steve two minutes after he talked, on the time thing. So I came in and my audition was to sit with Regis and to talk with him, and see how — because I’d be like a second banana. And I did what I’m doing with you. I’d put him on. I told him he was ugly, I don’t know what I — I just was doing Don Rickles. I was just like — I just can’t help it, it comes, it just comes out of my mouth like the music comes out of my brain. And so they liked me so they hired me. And the wildest thing, I wouldn’t go unless they gave me a 26 week contract. Because that’s how usually — the run of the show is usually 26 weeks in those days, instead of 13, 26.
